distribution.note: Kommands ships two builds from one codebase: a hosted web app and a standalone Wails v2 desktop app. Only the first exists today, which is why kind is still vite-web and health.commands is JS-only. When the Go shell lands, kind becomes vite-web+wails-desktop and health.commands gains the Go checks (go vet, go test, and the Wails build) so /suite-kit:health and CI stop covering half the product. They are deliberately not declared yet: there is no go.mod, CI runs suite-check.py --require-runnable, and a check that cannot run reports skip - which this repo treats as a failure rather than as green. Declaring them early would invert that.

minecraft.dataSource: misode/mcmeta, pinned by version-summary tag (1.21.1-summary), never by branch

invariants.name: no hardcoded game values
invariants.diagnosis: A game value was inlined instead of read from the version registry. Minecraft identifiers are versioned data — an item that exists in 1.21.1 may not exist in another version, and a literal silently ships the wrong value. Legitimate exception: the bare 'minecraft:' namespace prefix being constructed by a serializer. Judge by whether a specific entity, item, or enchantment is named — 'minecraft:' alone is fine, 'minecraft:diamond_sword' is not. Test files are excluded: a serializer fixture asserts literal expected command text, so the identifiers in it are the thing under test rather than a value that should have come from a registry. The rule is about components and serializers reaching for a literal instead of the version's data; a fixture that did that would not be a fixture. Canonical fixtures and their provenance live in docs/minecraft-versions.md.

invariants.name: no version-number comparisons
invariants.diagnosis: Serializers must branch on version traits, never on version numbers. A version-literal comparison breaks silently the moment a version is added: the 1.21.2 attribute rename and the 1.21.5 enchantments flattening did not land together, so no ordering of version numbers describes them. Branch on the trait flag instead.

invariants.name: no literal hex or px in components
invariants.diagnosis: Runtime theming works by overriding custom properties on the root element. An inlined value silently opts that element out of theming, and the breakage only appears in a non-default theme — not the one being looked at while the code is written. Every value has a named token, including the awkward ones (9px, 0.5px, 10px radius). If a value seems missing, add a token; do not inline or approximate. src/previews is covered too: a preview module needs a colour as a *value* rather than a class, and the way to get one is to resolve the custom property at runtime — see voxelColor in src/previews/worldedit/shape/ShapePreview.tsx. A literal there would be outside the grep's old reach while being exactly the drift it exists to catch.

generated.diagnosis: A non-empty diff means either src/data/generated was hand-edited, or a generator change was committed without its regenerated output. Both are bugs: the hand edit is destroyed on the next run and the underlying issue survives. Fix the generator, regenerate, and commit both together. Regeneration is deterministic — same mcmeta tag in, same bytes out — so a diff without a generator or version change means something else is wrong. requiresNetwork is declared for the cold case only: the deriver caches each pinned tag under .cache/mcmeta, so a warm run never reaches the network and CI restores that cache keyed on the tag.

A non-empty diff means either src/styles/tokens.css was hand-edited, or tokens.source.json was refreshed without regenerating. Both are bugs, for the same reason as gen:commands. Unlike that generator, this one reads a committed local file — tokens.source.json — so it works offline and has no legitimate skip.
